_comment: Editor UI metadata for MPC SOS Fade — labels, groups, plain-English descriptions, the 'essentials' (core) flag, conditional visibility (show_if), toggle option labels, and tuning guides. Read by the command-center scanner (strategies/python/<pkg>/<pkg>.meta.json) and overlaid onto the schema built from SosFadeConfig. UI ONLY: it never touches a trade decision or the source hash, so editing it needs no re-parity — but DO click Scan Strategies after editing. Param order here is the canonical UI order. Every show_if below was verified against the code, not assumed: exec_fvg_deep_only deliberately has NO condition (it still filters which FVGs qualify when Require FVG is off), and div_rsi_len/div_pivot_len have none either (they drive the divergence that ARMS the setup, which show_div does not gate — show_div only gates the veto and the live DIV flag). LABELS AND DESCRIPTIONS ARE SHARED WITH THE PINE (2026-08-02): every `label` here is byte-identical to that input's title in indicators/strategies/mpc_strategy.pine (minus Pine's leading '   ↳ ' indent marker), and every `desc` is that input's tooltip verbatim. One parameter, one name, one explanation, two UIs. Change a label or a desc and change the Pine in the same commit, or the two panels start teaching different things. The ONE allowed deviation is a suffix stating a fact true only of THIS runner — exec_conf_sz carries '(not supported)' because the Sniper-Zone entry is Pine-only. COPY STYLE (2026-08-10, Aaron's call): every desc is SHORT and PLAIN — what the setting does, what each choice means, and the one fact that changes the decision. No measurement dumps, no trade counts, no R figures, no dates, no file references: the strategy detail page is for reading, and the evidence behind a default lives in this package's CLAUDE.md and its optimization doc. Same rule for `edge` and `steps`.
edge: It trades reversals, but only once the market has proved the turn. First price runs the stops past a recent high or low. Then structure breaks the other way, which is the confirmation. Then it waits for a deep pullback and leaves a limit order sitting there — it never chases. Most of the money comes from the part of the trade that is left to run.

steps.label: 01 · Arm
steps.title: Something runs out of steam
steps.detail: Price runs the stops past a recent high or low. That is what puts a setup on the watchlist. A momentum divergence at an extreme can do it too, but that is off by default.

steps.label: 02 · Confirm
steps.title: Structure breaks the other way
steps.detail: The market breaks back the other way soon after. Without that the setup is only a guess, so it never arms.

steps.label: 03 · Zone
steps.title: Wait for the pullback
steps.detail: Price comes back deep into the move and a gap left behind sits in the same place. A limit order rests there and waits to be filled. It is never a chase.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Let it run
steps.detail: Touching the first target moves the stop to breakeven, so the trade can no longer lose. By default nothing is banked early — the whole position rides out on the trailing stop.

params.name: exec_arm_div
params.label: Arm on RSI divergence
params.desc: Lets a momentum divergence start a setup. If this and the sweep trigger are both off, nothing ever trades. It does not control the veto — that has its own switch.

params.name: exec_arm_sweep
params.label: Arm on liquidity sweep
params.desc: Lets a run on the stops past a recent high or low start a setup. Turn it off, leaving divergence on, to read divergence-started setups on their own.

params.name: aplus_window
params.label: Max time: sweep → SOS (minutes)
params.desc: How long a stop run stays valid while it waits for structure to confirm. In practice a break the other way is what really cancels it, so this only clears out very old ones. 4320 = 3 days.
guide: Only fresh signals count — fewer setups
An old signal can still trigger days later

params.name: exec_aplus
params.label: Trade A+ setups
params.desc: On = the main reversal setup trades normally. Off = it never fires. Turn it off with B-Leg on to read the B leg on its own.

params.name: exec_bleg
params.label: Trade B-Leg setups
params.desc: Adds a second setup: when a reversal never gets its pullback and the market runs on instead, this waits for the pullback to arrive late and buys it there. The main setup has first claim. Off by default.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: On = long setups may trade. Off = shorts only.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: On = short setups may trade. Off = longs only.

params.name: exec_req_fvg
params.label: Require an FVG in the zone
params.desc: On = only trade when there is a gap in the pullback zone. Off = trade the pullback on its own, at the 0.618 level. Off does not switch off the gap rules below — a gap still prices the entry when there is one.

params.name: exec_nogap_arm
params.label: ↳ No-FVG entries need
params.desc: Which no-gap setups may still trade when a gap is not required. Any = all of them. Sweep + RSI div = only the ones with both signals behind the turn. Lab only — this setting is not on the TradingView chart.

params.name: exec_poi_source
params.label: Zone the entry reads (lab only)
params.desc: Which kind of zone the entry price is read off. FVG is the shipped rule. The order-block modes were tested and did not earn their place; they are kept so anyone can re-check that. Lab only — only FVG exists on the TradingView chart.

params.name: exec_ob_deepen
params.label: Order block deeper than the entry → rest on the block
params.desc: On = when an order block sits deeper than the entry, move the order down onto it. A better price and a tighter stop, paid for in trades that never fill. Tested and rejected. Lab only.

params.name: exec_fvg_deep_only
params.label: Gap must sit fully past 0.5
params.desc: On = the whole gap must sit in the deep half of the pullback. Off = any gap touching the zone counts. On is stricter and takes fewer setups.

params.name: exec_fvg_pre_zone
params.label: Gap must pre-date the zone
params.desc: On = the gap only counts if it was already there before price pulled back this far. A gap left by the reversal candle itself is the move confirming itself.

params.name: exec_fib_overlap
params.label: Gap on a fib → enter on the fib
params.desc: Fires when a fib level sits inside the gap. On = rest the order on that level instead of at the edge of the gap, so it sits inside the gap rather than in front of it.

params.name: exec_fib_deep_edge
params.label: Floating gap → its own deep edge
params.desc: For a gap that holds no fib level and sits deeper than 0.618. On = rest the order at the far edge of the gap. It is the one deep rule that always fills, and it tested worse than the rule below. It overrides the two rules below.

params.name: exec_fib_nearest
params.label: Floating gap → nearest fib (either side)
params.desc: Same gap as the rule above. On = rest on whichever fib level is closest, above or below. It fixes a gap just short of a level being entered way back at the one before. Not free: when the deeper level wins, the order sits past the gap and a setup that only tags the gap never fills.

params.name: exec_deep_fib
params.label: Floating gap → nearest fib shallower
params.desc: The older, one-sided version of the two rules above, kept so old results still reproduce. It only ever looks at the level just above the gap, however much closer the one below is. Only used with both rules above off.

params.name: exec_conf_sz
params.label: Allow Sniper Zone as entry confirmation (not supported)
params.desc: Not supported in this bot — leave it off. Turning it on changes nothing on a lab run, and the TradingView comparison refuses an export taken with it on.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. Position size is worked back from this and the stop distance, so a tighter stop buys a bigger position at the same risk.
guide: Smaller swings, slower growth
Bigger swings — 10% is already aggressive

params.name: exec_sl_level
params.label: Stop fib level (deep side of 0.5)
params.desc: How far back the stop sits. 0.886 is the tested default. 1.0 is the widest and the safest. The three tighter levels can put the stop almost on top of the entry, which blows up the position size, so turn on the minimum stop distance first. Custom takes any level you type.

params.name: exec_sl_custom
params.label: Custom stop fib level
params.desc: Type your own stop level, used when the setting above is Custom. Deeper, towards 1.0, is the safe direction: a wider stop and a smaller position. Shallower than 0.886 is the dangerous half — turn on the minimum stop distance first. Lab only.
guide: Tighter stop, bigger position, less room to be right
Wider stop, smaller position, more room

params.name: exec_sl_deep
params.label: Entries at 0.786 or deeper stop at 1.0
params.disable_note: No effect — the stop is already 1.0, so both states place it in the same spot.
params.desc: On = an entry that fills at 0.786 or deeper puts its stop right back at the start of the move instead. That gives it room, because those entries otherwise have very little behind them, but it costs money on every trade it touches.

params.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
params.label: Stop buffer beyond the level (ticks)
params.desc: Extra room beyond the stop level, in ticks, so a wick through it does not take you out.
guide: Stop sits exactly on the level
More room for wicks, wider risk per trade

params.name: exec_min_stop_mode
params.label: Minimum stop distance
params.desc: Skip a setup whose stop sits closer to the entry than the floor below. Size is risk divided by stop distance, so a stop that collapses onto the entry does not risk less — it builds a huge position. Percent of price keeps scaling as gold rises; ATR is the wrong tool here, because the dangerous stops appear on quiet bars.

params.name: exec_min_stop_val
params.label: Minimum stop floor (unit = mode above)
params.desc: The floor itself. The unit follows the setting above — a percent, dollars of price, or an ATR multiple. Higher refuses more setups.
guide: Almost nothing is refused
Refuses real trades, not just dangerous ones

params.name: exec_tp1_pct
params.label: TP1 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the first target banks. 0 = bank nothing and ride it all, which tested best. The target still matters at 0 — touching it is what moves the stop to breakeven.
guide: More size left for the runner
Bank more early, smaller runner

params.name: exec_tp2_pct
params.label: TP2 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the second target banks. 0 = bank nothing. Touching it still lifts the stop and hands the rest to the trail.
guide: Bigger runner
Bank more at TP2, smaller runner

params.name: exec_be_buf_tk
params.label: Breakeven buffer (ticks)
params.desc: The breakeven stop sits this far past the entry, so a scratch still covers costs. It is also why TradingView reports no breakevens — those exits book a few cents, so it files them as wins. The trade label counts them honestly.
guide: True breakeven
Locks in more, stopped out sooner

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the stop follows the trade once the second target is hit, and which setting below is live. Fixed step is a plain dollar grid. Structure parks the stop at the last swing, which breathes with the trend but hands a lot back at the turn. Structure + ratchet is the default and banks more of each run.
guide: Fixed step — simplest, and the worst of the three
Structure + ratchet — keeps more of each run

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: Used by both structure methods. The trailing stop sits this many ticks beyond the last swing, so a wick through it does not clip you.
guide: Tight to the swing — clipped by wicks
Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

params.name: exec_trail_pct
params.label: Runner ratchet step (% of price)
params.desc: How big each step of the trailing stop is, as a percent of price. A percent rather than dollars, because gold has run from 1,500 to 3,400 and a fixed amount means something different at each end. Too small and it starts cutting winners short.
guide: Too small — cuts winners short
Too big — barely does anything

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: The step size in dollars. Read by two settings, so it is never greyed out: the fixed-step trail, and the one-step-behind stop floor. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 50 pips = 5.0.
guide: Tighter trail — banks sooner, cuts runners short
Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: Where the stop jumps to the moment the second target is hit, before the trail takes over. TP1 price is tight and can scratch the trade on the first pullback. Breakeven gives it the most room. One trail step behind keeps it just under the best price seen. The trail can still tighten past this.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

params.name: exec_time_stop_mode
params.label: Time stop
params.desc: Close a trade that has been open longer than the hours set below. Before TP1 only is the tested setting: it fires only while the trade has never reached the first target, so it never cuts a winner. Always closes on the clock alone, winners included. Off closes nothing.
guide: Off — the clock never closes a trade
Always — the clock closes winners too

params.name: exec_time_stop_hrs
params.label: Time stop (hours)
params.desc: How long a trade may stay open, in hours, weekends included. Anything from about 24 to 40 hours gives the same answer, so read it as a range rather than an exact number. Below 16 hours it starts cutting winners, because the losers here die faster than the winners do.
guide: Cuts winners as well as losers
Fires on almost nothing

params.name: exec_close_opp_sos
params.label: Close on opposite SOS
params.desc: On = close the trade early if structure breaks back the other way, on the view that the reversal has failed. Off = let the stop or a target resolve every trade.

params.name: exec_secondary
params.label: Secondary re-entries (1m SOS)
params.desc: Adds a second entry off the 1-minute chart: once the first trade is safe at breakeven and price falls back into the zone, it re-enters with a tighter stop for the same targets. It fires about eight times in eight years and nearly all of the result is one trade. Lab only, and slow to run.

params.name: exec_sec_once_per_setup
params.label: One re-entry per primary
params.desc: How often one setup may be re-entered. On = once. Off = once per 1-minute signal, which is what once let a single setup be re-entered twice about an hour and a half apart. It resets on a fresh break of structure. Lab only.

params.name: exec_sec_retrace
params.label: Secondary entry retrace
params.desc: How deep the 1-minute re-entry waits before its order fills. 0 enters straight away on the signal. The stop sits in the same place either way, so entering earlier means a wider stop, a smaller position and less room to the targets. Lab only.

params.name: show_div
params.label: Track RSI divergence (REQUIRED — arms setups + veto)
params.desc: Spots momentum running out: price makes a lower low while momentum makes a higher low from oversold, or the mirror at a high. It confirms a few bars after the actual turn. Entries need this — turning it off disables both the divergence trigger and the veto.

params.name: div_rsi_len
params.label: RSI length
params.desc: The momentum lookback. 14 is standard. Shorter reacts faster and finds more signals.
guide: Twitchier RSI, more divergences
Smoother RSI, fewer but cleaner

params.name: div_pivot_len
params.label: Pivot width (bars)
params.desc: How many bars either side of a turn confirm it. This is also the delay — nothing can print until that many bars after the turn. Wider means fewer and cleaner signals.
guide: Confirms sooner, more noise
Confirms later, only real pivots

params.name: div_valid_bars
params.label: Divergence valid for (bars)
params.desc: How long a divergence keeps counting once it prints.
guide: Expires fast
Stays live longer

params.name: div_veto
params.label: Veto setups on extreme/divergence
params.desc: On = block a long while a bearish divergence is live or momentum is extremely overbought, and the mirror for shorts. This is where the veto is built; the entry setting only decides whether entries obey it.

params.name: exec_respect_veto
params.label: Respect divergence/extreme veto
params.desc: On = entries obey the veto. The veto itself is built in the RSI divergence section — switch it off there and this has nothing to obey.

params.name: div_extreme_ob
params.label: Extreme overbought
params.desc: Momentum at or above this counts as extremely overbought, which blocks longs. Higher blocks less often.
guide: Vetoes longs more often
Only vetoes at a true extreme

params.name: div_extreme_os
params.label: Extreme oversold
params.desc: Momentum at or below this counts as extremely oversold, which blocks shorts. Lower blocks less often.
guide: Only vetoes at a true extreme
Vetoes shorts more often

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-17:00 NY)
params.desc: On = no new entries in the last hour before the daily close. Gold closes at 17:00 New York and reopens at 18:00, so a trade opened late can be gapped out over the break.

params.name: flat_by_close
params.label: Flat by close
params.desc: Close everything before the daily close instead of holding overnight. Off by default, and that was tested: holding makes far more money, because the few trades that run overnight are the big winners and the overnight fee is tiny by comparison.

params.name: flat_by_close_min
params.label: Flatten this early
params.desc: How many minutes before the daily close to force everything flat.
guide: Hold closer to the bell
Exit earlier, more of the close avoided

params.name: exec_htf_weekly
params.label: Weekly bias requirement
params.desc: Whether the weekly trend has to agree with the trade. Ignore = no filter. Must agree = weekly matches the trade. Must not oppose = neutral is fine. Must oppose = weekly has to be against it.
guide: Ignore = no filter, trade every setup
Must agree = only with the weekly trend

params.name: exec_htf_daily
params.label: Daily bias requirement
params.desc: The same four choices, judged on the daily trend. Ignore = off.

params.name: exec_htf_exhaust_only
params.label: Only fade HTF exhaustion, not breakouts
params.desc: On = skip a reversal that fights a fresh higher-timeframe breakout, while still taking one that fades an exhausted move. Off = no higher-timeframe filter, and the setting below greys out.

params.name: exec_htf_source
params.label: HTF exhaustion source
params.desc: Which higher timeframe the breakout check reads. Weekly blocks the fewest trades. Either blocks the most.

params.name: exec_scratch_r
params.label: Scratch band
params.desc: Reporting only — it never changes a trade. A trade that finishes this close to breakeven is counted as a scratch instead of a win or a loss. It matters because this bot scratches a lot.
guide: Fewer trades called scratch
More near-breakeven trades called scratch

params.name: alert_resting_fib
params.label: Announce a resting limit at fib
params.desc: Reporting only — it never changes a trade, and the order is still placed the moment the setup arms. It decides WHEN the signals channel tells you a limit is pending: price has to retrace this far back down the leg first. At the default the order is announced once price has given back 23.6% of the move, instead of the moment it is placed — which can be hours and tens of dollars before price could reach it. Must stay under 0.5, because every fill happens at 0.5 or deeper and the message has to go out before any trade can.
guide: Told sooner, further from the entry
Told later, closer to the entry

params.name: fill_model
params.label: Fill model
params.desc: How fills are priced. Bar matches the TradingView chart and charges nothing, which is the mode used to check the two against each other. Tick uses real bid and ask prices with real costs. Use tick for any number you want to trust.

params.name: account_profile
params.label: Account profile
params.desc: Whose costs to charge in tick mode. vantage_demo is the broker the backtests are measured on, so results line up with the TradingView chart. The puprime ones are the live broker, kept for reference. Ignored in bar mode.

params.name: symbol
params.label: Broker symbol
params.desc: The symbol the price data is pulled from. Vantage gold is XAUUSD, with no suffix. Ignored in bar mode.
